rawCommits.subject: fix(sessions): keep new chat highlighted across optimistic→real swap
rawCommits.body:
After SessionReady, `useNewSessionUrlSync` did two things in sequence:

  1. `optimisticRow.swap(<real-id>)` — synchronously rewrote the
     `optimistic:<uuid>` row in `sessionsBySurface` to the
     server-assigned UUID via Zustand `setState`.
  2. `setSearchParams({ session: <real-id> })` — queued a React
     Router navigate.

`SessionsList`'s `effectiveSelectedSessionId` only had two cases — URL
session, or fall back to the optimistic row. The window between those
two writes (and any subsequent render where the router state hadn't
propagated through `useSearchParams` yet — back/forward, suspended tab,
etc.) had neither: the row was no longer `optimistic:` and `?session=`
hadn't landed, so the just-created session visibly appeared at the top
of the list with its server-generated title but read as unselected.
The user reported this as "after sending message in new session, still
does not select it in the css".

Add a third fallback: when the URL has no `?session=` and no optimistic
row exists, highlight `titledRows[0]` — the newest row in the surface.
The surfaces are stored in `sortSessionsDesc` order from
`loadAgentSessions` / `loadProjectSessions`, and `addOptimisticSession`
stamps `started_at` at insert time, so the just-swapped real-id row
always sorts to the top across the swap window. Pre-swap, the
optimistic branch still wins; once the URL settles, the explicit
`selectedSessionId` branch wins again.

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>
rawCommits.cleanSubject: keep new chat highlighted across optimistic→real swap

rawCommits.subject: feat(swarm): auto-recover once on initial-provision failure and surface swarm error
rawCommits.body:
When a brand-new remote agent's background readiness wait timed out or
saw `state: error`, the only effect was a `warn!` in the desktop log:
the agent stayed in `provisioning`, the UI sat indefinitely on
"Starting up...", and the user had to manually click Recovery (often
not even knowing the agent was stuck). The cause string supplied by
aura-swarm (e.g. an `Unschedulable` PodScheduled message) was also
dropped because `SwarmAgentStateResponse` only deserialized `state`,
so any error event the gateway emitted was reduced to a generic
"entered error state".

Changes:

- Widen `SwarmAgentStateResponse` to include `error_message` and
  carry the optional reason through `SwarmAgentReadyError::ErrorState`
  and `PollOutcome::Errored`.
- Replace the inert `warn!()` branches in `spawn_swarm_readiness_check`
  with `auto_recover_after_initial_failure`, which broadcasts an
  `auto_recover/starting` event, runs the existing
  `recover_remote_agent_pipeline` exactly once, and on failure
  broadcasts a terminal `state: "error", phase: "startup_failed"`
  carrying both the original swarm reason and the recovery error so
  the StatusCard exits the indeterminate provisioning state and shows
  the manual Recovery action.
- Update `handle_recovery_readiness_error` to embed the swarm-supplied
  reason in both the broadcast banner and the `ApiError`, so the
  manual Recovery click also surfaces the descriptive cause.
- Pass enough context (cloned `AppState`, `Arc<NetworkClient>`,
  `NetworkAgent`) through `BackgroundReadinessTask` to invoke recovery
  from the spawned task.
- Add `starting` and `startup_failed` entries to the StatusCard
  `PHASE_NOTICES` so the UI labels match the new broadcast phases.

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>
rawCommits.cleanSubject: auto-recover once on initial-provision failure and surface swarm error

rawCommits.body:
The publish-release-changelog-media workflow calls three different paid
APIs (Anthropic, OpenAI, Browser Use). When one runs out of credits, the
previous wording made it ambiguous which account actually needed a top-up
- e.g. "You need at least $1.00 in credits. Current balance: $0.34" with

  at least $1.00 in credits. Current balance: $0.34

rawCommits.subject: chore(changelog-media): downgrade Browser Use credit-low to a warning
rawCommits.body:
Previously a low Browser Use balance crashed the entire
publish-release-changelog-media workflow at the first capture
attempt - even though the rest of the pipeline (planner, report,
manifest) had nothing to do with that account. The pipeline is
already best-effort (the desktop release and text changelog ship
before this workflow even runs), so the right behavior is to skip
the Browser Use flow for the cycle and exit cleanly.

runChangelogMediaEvaluation now wraps the runBrowserUseTaskImpl call:
when wrapProviderError raises a `[Browser Use]` credit-low error
(providerCreditError === true && provider === "browser-use"), the
current candidate becomes a `blocked` result with the credit message
in `blockers[]`, a `browser-use-credit-exhausted` progress event
fires, and a flag short-circuits every remaining candidate so the
SDK isn't called again. Non-credit Browser Use failures still throw.

The report and stdout summary now carry `browserUseCreditExhausted`,
`browserUseCreditMessage`, and `counts.captureSkippedForCredits`, and
the script exits 0 - so the downstream "Publish accepted media into
gh-pages" step finds an empty manifest and no-ops cleanly instead of
the whole job going red.

Regression test plans two candidates, has runBrowserUseTaskImpl
throw a credit-tagged error, and asserts the SDK is called exactly
once while both candidates land as blocked with the credit blocker.

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>

rawCommits.subject: fix(channel): stop stable build from running as Dev via feature unification
rawCommits.body:
The published "AURA" installer was silently running as a Dev binary at
runtime - same single-instance mutex, same `aura-dev` data dir, "AURA
Dev" window title, in-app updater disabled - because `aura-os-core`
declared `default = ["dev-channel"]` and every library crate depended
on it without `default-features = false`. Cargo feature unification
re-activated `aura-os-core/dev-channel` for every workspace build,
including the release pipeline's `--no-default-features --features
stable-channel` build of `aura-os-desktop`, so `Channel::current()`
always resolved to Dev. Result: `cargo run -p aura-os-desktop` and the
installed prod binary both held `Local\com.aura.desktop-dev.single-instance`
and the second to start logged "another Aura instance is already
running" and exited.

- Drop `aura-os-core`'s default channel; add `default-features = false`
  to every internal `aura-os-core = { path = "..." }` dep across 17
  workspace crates so library deps can no longer pin the workspace to
  a channel.
- Flip `Channel::current()` to prefer `stable-channel` when both
  features happen to be active, with Dev as the bare-library fallback
  so plain `cargo test` keeps writing to the dev tree.
- Add a `--print-channel` flag to `aura-os-desktop` that prints
  `channel=Stable ...` (or `channel=Dev ...`) and exits before any
  startup side-effects; wire `scripts/ci/verify-desktop.mjs` to run
  the just-built stable binary with it and fail the release if the
  binary doesn't self-report Stable, so this regression can't return
  silently.
- Add a one-shot recovery in `init_data_dirs`: on Stable, if
  `~/<localdata>/aura-dev` has user state and `~/<localdata>/aura/store`
  doesn't, move the dev tree over (same for `~/.aura-dev/skills` ->
  `~/.aura/skills`), gated by a `.migrated-from-aura-dev` marker so it
  runs exactly once. Covered by unit tests for the four edge cases.
- Update doc comments in `aura-os-core/src/channel.rs`, the two binary
  Cargo.toml feature sections, and the release-stable/release-nightly
  workflows to spell out the new invariant: libraries opt out of
  defaults, the CI `--print-channel` assertion enforces it.

Verified locally: `..\.aura-shared-target\release\aura-os-desktop.exe
--print-channel` prints `channel=Stable data_dir=aura ...
window_title="AURA" mutex=Local\com.aura.desktop.single-instance
desktop_port=19847 updater_enabled=true`, while the debug build prints
`channel=Dev data_dir=aura-dev ... desktop_port=19848`.

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>
rawCommits.cleanSubject: stop stable build from running as Dev via feature unification

rendered.title: A searchable agent picker, a stable channel rescue, and sharper release diagnostics
rendered.intro: Today's nightly centers on a redesigned project agent picker — now a searchable, keyboard-driven list backed by the full org fleet — plus a critical fix that stops stable installers from silently running as Dev. Smaller polish lands across chat, sessions, the 3D viewer, the marketplace, and the release-media pipeline.

entries.title: Searchable agent picker replaces the project sidebar's card grid
entries.summary: The project '+' flow now opens a single keyboard-driven picker with a Standard Agent shortcut, plus fixes for new-chat selection, installer theming, and remote-agent provisioning.

items.text: Replaced the Add-Agent card grid with a Telegram-style searchable list: an autofocused search input, a Standard Agent row at the top, live name/role filtering, arrow-key + Enter navigation, and per-row spinners during create. The redundant '+ Create New Agent' footer and its editor modal are gone — a generic agent now spawns with one Enter inside the picker.
Newly created chat sessions now stay highlighted in the sidebar across the optimistic-to-real ID swap, closing a window where the just-sent session briefly read as unselected after SessionReady.

Remote agents that fail their initial provisioning readiness check now auto-recover once and, if recovery fails, surface the actual swarm error (e.g. an Unschedulable pod reason) in the StatusCard instead of sitting forever on "Starting up...".

Chat attachments now accept .json and .sql files, and the Windows installer correctly stages its themed dark/light bitmaps from $PLUGINSDIR with the dark title-bar hook applied to the uninstaller as well.

entries.title: Sidebar navigation, 3D export, and a CEO-only permissions correction
entries.summary: Mid-day polish across the Projects sidebar and chat, a GLB download in the 3D viewer, a tightened default-permissions rule, and a Windows installer build fix.

items.text: Projects sidebar now auto-expands to reveal the active agent when navigating in from elsewhere, session rows display their project name when results span multiple projects, and the Add Agent modal no longer gets trapped in a stale busy state that blocked Close, Escape, and Create.
Chat now shows a helpful error when a message is sent to an agent not assigned to a project, instead of failing silently in the stream lifecycle.
Aura 3D's WebGL viewer gained a Download button on its toolbar so users can save the generated GLB directly, using the same desktop-webview-friendly anchor pattern as Gallery and Model3DBlock.

Reverted an over-broad rule that had been promoting every empty capability bundle to full_access — non-CEO agents now keep their empty bundle and opt in through the Permissions tab, while the CEO bootstrap and project-scoped self-caps are preserved.
Windows installer build no longer aborts in makensis: the uninstaller's GUI-init callback is now correctly prefixed with `un.` so MUI_LANGUAGE expansion succeeds.

entries.title: Agent picker stability and Projects entry-point polish
entries.summary: Follow-up fixes that lock the new picker's size, broaden it to the full org fleet, and restore predictable defaults around the Projects sidebar.

items.text: The project Add-Agent picker now queries the full org fleet (matching the Agents app sidebar) instead of only the current user's authored agents, and a 360px-floor `.pickerBody` prevents the modal from resizing between loading, loaded, and post-selection states. Recently selected rows stay visible during the create+handoff transition to eliminate the empty-state flash.
The agent context-menu action in the Projects sidebar is now labeled "Remove from Project" to match the existing modal copy and make project-scoped removal unambiguous.

Projects now reliably lands on the Terminal tab on entry: the shared sidekick store was being polluted by Tasks and the spec-generation stream, so ProjectMainPanel forces `setActiveTab("terminal")` once per mount while still respecting later user navigation.

entries.title: Stable channel rescue and resilient changelog-media pipeline
entries.summary: A long-running release-quality thread: the stable installer was silently running as a Dev binary, and the changelog-media workflow learned to identify and tolerate credit exhaustion at third-party providers.

items.text: Fixed a Cargo feature-unification bug that had been shipping the "AURA" stable installer as a Dev binary in disguise — same dev mutex, `aura-dev` data dir, "AURA Dev" window title, and disabled in-app updater. Every internal `aura-os-core` dep now opts out of default features, `Channel::current()` prefers `stable-channel` when both are active, and a new `--print-channel` self-check in `scripts/ci/verify-desktop.mjs` fails the release lane if the built binary doesn't self-report Stable. A one-shot, marker-guarded migration moves user state from `aura-dev` to `aura` for affected installs.

Every paid-API failure in the publish-release-changelog-media workflow (Anthropic, OpenAI, Browser Use) now flows through a shared `wrapProviderError` helper that prefixes the failing provider and names the env var to top up, so CI logs are unambiguous about which account needs attention.

A low Browser Use balance no longer reds the entire media workflow: the first credit-low error converts the candidate to a `blocked` result, short-circuits remaining candidates, emits a `browser-use-credit-exhausted` progress event, and exits 0 so the downstream gh-pages publish no-ops cleanly.

entries.title: 3D style-lock restoration and marketplace creator avatars
entries.summary: Late-day product touches: re-applying the 3D style lock only where it belongs, and giving marketplace cards a recognizable author.

items.text: Restored `STYLE_LOCK_SUFFIX` on the implicit 3D-source image paths — chat 3D mode's image step (in both `useChatStream` and `useAgentChatStream`) and the standalone Aura 3D ImageGeneration flow — while leaving chat /image and all other free-form image sends untouched.

Marketplace agent talent cards now show the creator's avatar and name as a third column on the Tasks/Revenue stats row, plumbed through the existing MarketplaceAgent DTO instead of per-card client lookups, with the shared Avatar fallback for creators without a photo.

highlights: Project agent picker reborn as a searchable Telegram-style list
Stable installer no longer ships as a Dev binary in disguise
Remote agents auto-recover once on provisioning failure
Release-media pipeline names the provider that ran out of credits
